Q1: Nitrous acid exhibits known hazards (Tier 1) for environmental and dermal/eye effects based on official GHS classifications. It also has expanded perspectives (Tier 2) regarding carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards. However, there are significant data deficiencies (Tier 4) concerning its endocrine disruption, inhalation, oral, and organ/systemic hazards.
Q2: Nitrous acid is not currently found on any established lists of concern or low hazard. This absence may be attributed to a lack of extensive study or its infrequent common use, especially considering the significant data deficiencies identified across several of its hazard classes.
Q3: Nitrous acid is relatively well-characterized in scientific literature, with 10,000 references in SciFinder, placing it significantly above the median for our specialized dataset of approximately 3,000 petrochemicals. Its molecular formula (HNO2) is clearly defined, and it is categorized as a Small Molecule; however, a substantial portion of its hazard profile remains data deficient, with four out of seven hazard classes assigned a Tier 4 rating.
